A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frogs in the e-waste recycling areas had been exposed to high levels of legacy and emerging organphosphorus flame retardant and plasticizer contaminants.
PFRs and their precursors were more accumulated in male frogs than in female frogs, and the levels of PFRs were higher in gonads than in eggs.
the sex-specific accumulation in frogs could be due to the maternal transfer of PFRs, whereas that of plasticizers could be attributed to the paternal transfer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sex-specific accumulation and maternal transfer of PFRs, and paternal transfer of plasticizers, in frogs should be further considered in risk assessment and environmental monitoring.
